This isn’t just parenting—it’s a masterclass in systems dynamics that rewires how you approach *every* challenge, from work projects to community issues. ### 2. **Patience becomes a muscle, not just a virtue** You described " steady patience"—and that’s key. It’s not passive waiting; it’s active, *intentional* patience built through repeated practice. When you’re the one who must calmly navigate a tantrum while simultaneously prepping dinner and fielding a work email, you’re literally retraining your nervous system. This perspective spills into every part of life: you become less reactive, more grounded, and far more resilient in the face of chaos. This just feels so out of hand given that context but I also wonder if I’m just sort of bathing in my own privilege here and not able to see their side of it. Any thoughts?
